title: Formal analysis: worksheet and paper rules

cards.front: Name the 6 formal elements on the Kimbell worksheet.
cards.back:
One: Line
Two: Shape
Three: Color
Four: Tone
Five: Space
Six: Texture

What: Visible and implied lines (a pointing hand, figures all looking one way)
How: Direction, thickness, quality (thin, jagged, fuzzy)
Role: How lines connect, divide, define forms, or guide the eye
Rule: Always give location words: left, right, top, center

What: Each object's shape and the shapes of whole groupings
Role: How shapes balance, organize, or carry meaning
Class example: Leonardo's triangle of Christ in the Last Supper = divine perfection

What: The overall palette (warm, cool, earth tones, primary, secondary, pastel)
Role: Repeated or contrasting hues that connect objects and move the eye

What: Light, shadow, highlights, contrast
Light source: Where it comes from, and why you think so
Mood: Lighting sets the mood, which is not the same as your personal emotion

What: Depth, distance between objects, how 3-D things look
Terms to use: Linear perspective, atmospheric perspective, foreshortening, modeling, scale

Actual: The paint surface: visible brushstrokes vs. smooth with no trace of the hand
Implied: How surfaces are made to look (fuzzy peach, hard cold glass)
Rule: Say exactly why it looks that way. She grades this one hard

cards.front: Description vs. composition: what's the difference?
cards.back:
Description: What is depicted: subject, style adjective (realistic, idealized, painterly), setting, details specific to this painting
Composition: How it's arranged and how the eye moves: balance, foreground/background, groupings, halves or quarters, entry point, path of the eye

cards.front: Which painting can you pick at the Kimbell?
cards.back:
Rule: A painting made before 1900
Not allowed: Sculpture, even if it's before 1900

cards.front: Which label info do you record, and what's a trap?
cards.back:
Record: Artist, title, artwork date (keep "circa"), medium
Trap: The artist's lifespan and the acquisition date are not the artwork's date
Trap: "Guest of Honor" (a loan) and "New Acquisition" are not the title
Order: Look at the painting first, read the label after

cards.front: How do you build the paper?
cards.back:
Thesis: Introduction with a thesis statement
Body: The three formal elements doing the most work, each backed by visual evidence
Goal: Your own interpretation of meaning. Just answering the worksheet prompts earns about a B

cards.front: Paper rules: what's required and what's banned?
cards.back:
Required: Prescribed formatting, numbered pages, "the viewer" instead of I/me/we
Banned: Quotations
AI: Say which program you used and exactly how it helped

Bring: Pencil (no pens), phone on silent for photos, comfortable shoes
Not allowed: Food, drinks, pets
Distance: About 3 feet from the art; don't lean in or touch
Meet: Outside, downstairs at the permanent-collection building (barrel vaults), side facing the Modern
